heard: You do not have to wait until 2061 to see Halley's comet. Most people believe the iconic traveler vanished after 1986 and will not return for decades. Halley takes about 76 years to orbit the sun, shedding dust and debris along its path. Every late October, Earth plows directly through this trail, igniting the Orionid meteor shower. These particles strike the upper atmosphere at a blistering 66 kilometers per second. That violent friction vaporizes the dust into incandescent trains, lingering for seconds to minutes. Halley even produces a second shower, the Ato Aquariads, crossing Earth's path every May. The famous traveler's ancient debris is already burning right above your head tonight.
differences: 'eta aquariids' heard as 'ato aquariads' after '2nd shower the'
